Inspired by recent roguelike classics, Katanaut offers a unique blend of high octane action and eerie cyberpunk aesthetics that cement it as a bespoke masterpiece in the genre. The variety of build options are vast enough to keep tens of hours of playthroughs unique without feeling like you're repeating the same things over and over again. (Full review coming soon.)

完美解决了传统肉鸽操作感不够爽，武士零重复游玩度不高的缺点 整体操作是以武士零为基础，基本上80%都是照搬的（但是好玩，并非是在鉴抄） 然后肉鸽的思路是用的死亡细胞，例如地图规划，传送门，红绿紫三选一，基地内细胞解锁属性和图纸等等 整体缝的非常好，48这个价位绝对值得一玩，就是一个略微不满意的地方，武器如果没有击杀敌人或者打出暴击的话命中反馈非常弱希望这个可以改改加强下反馈，总体来讲就像评论区里的一个老哥说的那样，绝对不辱katana之名 9/12： 玩了6个小时后发现平衡有点烂啊，看的出来开发商想做个法术的BP，可问题是法术（以太）词条和技能一个比一个烂啊，刀也是，初始刀一刀扣5耐力，但是以太刀全是10以上的耐力消耗，目前解锁到第五把刀，一刀要消耗19点耐力，太恐怖了

Even though I'm not a fan of the genre, I had a great time playing. The gameplay is fun and addictive in a way that every playthrough is a bit different due to the rouge-lite mechanics, Like many reviews say, it really does feel a lot like a hack-n-slash-Dead Space. Really engaging gameplay, lore, writing. There's also a great amount of replayability without the needless backtracking due to randomized events. The sense of progression is just right and I'm still having fun, which is nice.

讲真的，这个游戏的打击以及节奏都把控的很不错，尤其是杀完敌人的时候空间站充满的血浆很爽，但游戏的结尾却给我一种戛然而止的感觉，这游戏难道会有dlc会有第二部吗？ 游戏的平衡一言难尽，游戏虽然给玩家提供了许多种不同的技能，但称得上好用且玩得舒服的就那几种，比如斩首是我非常爱使用的技能，其他技能我甚至看都不看就直接回收了（可能是我的问题吧） 游戏里你可以通过多种不同的事件来获取不同的刀，我只找到了一把控制时间的刀，但用起来..........一言难尽。 游戏不只是战斗爽，战斗中更是充满了作者一些小心思和巧妙有趣的事情，比如找到血祭坛防追杀，还有进入混沌传送门对战精英怪，或者在关卡里面撸猫，这些都给我充满了惊喜和探索乐趣，很难不夸赞和惊叹。 求你添加和人物立绘吧，重要人物就行！！！ 很棒的独立游戏，很多地方都可以看出来作者都是认真的做游戏。

[h1]刀枪并用，血肉横飞：浪客大闹寄生体空间站！[/h1] [h2]游戏推荐指数：★★★★★★★★★☆[/h2] [h3]前言[/h3] 一座没有了生息的空间站。 或者说，一座曾经满是生灵的空间站，如今已经完全没有了生息：因为上面还能够活动的，早已不是人类了。 而作为探索小队成员之一的你——浪客诺特，将要用你手上的刀，在这片地狱之中杀出一条血路、并逐步发掘整个事件背后的真相。 [h3]整体玩法[/h3] 本作的玩法是[b]经典的横版2D战斗[/b]，不过并不是固定的关卡内容，而是结合了一定的肉鸽元素，每次的关卡内容都是全新的。战斗系统上初始有着[b]主副两个武器槽[/b]，主武器固定是[b]武士刀[/b]（初始两把，一共六把可以选择），[b]副武器就比较多样化了，从简单的手枪、沙鹰到火力猛一点的霰弹枪、榴弹炮以及一些有着特殊功能武器譬如的传送飞刀、勾爪枪（可以发射钩索跨越地形）、格挡刀（功能就是字面意思）等等[/b]，副武器使用需要消耗[b]“弹药”[/b]（可以理解为能量，因为有些副武器不是枪），弹药在使用主武器砍敌人的时候会自动获得。其他的操作就比较常规了，有跳跃（可以二段跳）、冲刺，冲刺有短暂的无敌帧，除此之外还有[b]两个技能槽，可以在关卡内获取技能并装上。[/b] [h3]从未如此流畅的战斗！[/h3] 本作最值得称道的地方就是打击敌人时非常舒爽流畅，并且各种操作的衔接极其流畅，除了部分明确说了有释放延迟的技能外，大多数操作的前后摇都非常短，基本上连招想怎么接就怎么接，在跳跃和冲刺的任何时候都能平A和放技能，并且主武器的平A可以弹飞大部分诸如敌人的子弹之类的玩意儿，所以哪怕操作一般般只会咔咔咔一顿乱砍也有着非常棒的游戏体验。而要想玩得舒服点甚至于通关就要构思一下搭配了，[b]游戏中的伤害类型分为“动能”、“战斗”和“以太”[/b]，无论是主武器副武器还是技能都有其中的一至两个属性，而在探索中我们会找到各种强化注射剂，能够自行选择强化某个属性的伤害，因此假如武器技能都选择相同的伤害类型，强化起来就会比较高效。 [h3]局外强化[/h3] 再来聊聊本作的局外强化吧，[b]初始我们能够获得的主副武器以及技能都是有限的，很多都需要在战斗中发现，并在基地中研发，这样下一次进入战斗它们才会被加入随机池子里[/b]。另外战斗中获得的货币以及击败BOSS才有的高级货币可以强化自身的各种属性，譬如生命上限、弹药上限、体力、恢复剂使用次数等等，毕竟在本作中血量只有用恢复剂回复这一个方式，而恢复剂从地图中的箱子里爆出来的概率也并不高；又因为上面说的角色战斗性能很高的缘故，很多时候多一两滴血承受一下失误吃到的BOSS攻击就足以将其击败。 [h3]碎片化的剧情[/h3] 最后也简单谈谈剧情吧。本作的剧情除了整个故事的开端算是比较明朗、在游戏中有一段完整的动画展现的，其余基本都散落在各处，地图场景里的某个告示牌上、探索中遇到的npc的只言片语、一些触发得让人一头雾水的碎片剧情等等，诸如此类。不过这些倒也不重要，毕竟本作的游戏类型决定了只要它让人玩得足够爽就行了，其他什么的都很次要了。 [h3]其他[/h3] 另外还有关于本作[b]“血腥”[/b]的地方，其实笔者自己觉得还好，主要体现在基本上每一次攻击到敌人都会有血迹留在地图上，杀掉敌人后其身体的残肢也会简单地堆在地板上，因而经常一场大战下来整个空间站处处飘红，和打翻的番茄酱一样。兴许是最近笔者的压力有些大，几个小时打下来对这样的设计只感到解压，倒没有多少的生理不适。 [quote]欢迎关注『 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45525570/] 桃你欢心 [/url]』 [b] 桃影扶风评百戏，落墨如歌写人间[/b][/quote]

I want to like this game, I really do. But every time I go back and play it, I end up coming away from the game liking it less and less. There's some really critical issues with the gameplay that ends up just tanking the whole experience. The first and foremost issue is that enemy and boss design isn't great. From enemies that explode on death, to bosses that like to suddenly change attacks with little windup to really poor animations. The end result is that combat tends to just feel bad, and that's really bad when you're trying to be a similar game to Dead Cells. Dead Cells could also have visibility issues with combat at higher difficulties but this sort of amps things up 10x, because one moment you'll be mowing down hordes and then take chip damage from a zombie that swung at you obscured by the fifty other zombies nearby. This design also tends to leak into boss fights where they tend to have projectiles or a bunch of other stuff flying around the screen to make up for a really limited moveset. That issue also ties into the other half of why combat tends to feel bad, there's very little omph to combat. Enemies and even your own attacks have very little buildup and swings come out instantly. Without any weight to the things you do all of your weapons and skills tend to feel very same-y. That said, I think the aesthetic is great and I'm interested in where the story is going. But I can't really recommend it in this state as a fan of action games. It needs significant refinement and improvement. It has the content, just not the foundation.

[h3] You can read my other reviews [url=https://www.indiecornergames.com/] here! [/url] [/h3] [b] TL;RD [/b] Katanaut is a fun and technically solid game, but without that extra “spark” to set it apart from many similar titles already on the market. [h1] Full Review [/h1] Living surrounded by cosmic terrors is hardly anyone’s dream. However, for horror fans with a soft spot for roguelite action, Katanaut is a feast. The game is a curious fusion of Dead Cells and Dead Space, fittingly, they even share half their name, yet each follows a distinctly different style of gameplay. The former is rooted in the fast-paced, demanding roguelike genre, while the latter leans on iconic moments of suspense and horror in a third-person shooter perspective. Katanaut embraces a frantic pace, throwing the player into corridors swarming with enemies aboard a space station infested with bizarre creatures, each with unique attack patterns. The goal is simple: adapt to this blood-soaked environment, survive, and uncover the secrets behind the catastrophe that devastated the station. As you progress, secondary characters appear to aid Naut, the protagonist, along his path. Being a roguelite, progression unfolds through a well-branched skill tree, allowing the hero to grow stronger with every run. The arsenal evolves alongside this growth: two distinct katanas, one swift and mobility-focused, the other slower but devastating, are complemented by firearms with varied ammo types and firing modes. The sense of impact and the responsive controls stand out, offering precision and immediate feedback. While it doesn’t bring major innovations to the genre, Katanaut succeeds in creating a captivating universe where cyberpunk and horror intertwine, with neon-lit corridors splattered in blood at every new section. The art direction is consistent, featuring dramatic lighting and sound effects that heighten the tension. The electronic soundtrack, though understated, reinforces the oppressive atmosphere. Above all, it’s a fun and technically solid game, but without that extra “spark” to set it apart from many similar titles already on the market. Those seeking something entirely new may find it familiar. Still, for fans of the genre, especially players who enjoy demanding melee combat in a roguelite, Katanaut is a strong choice. Add to that a vast array of unlockables and achievements, and you have plenty of hours of “just one more run” replayability.

这游戏虽是可以，并且也是制作组的处女作。可以算是值得一试。但是我觉得有些问题存在，并且也是确确实实影响到游玩体验。所以如果能改变的话游戏体验可以好上许多； （1）.地图问题 1.在小地图问题存在重要资源，NPC和特殊房间内不在地图内显示。从而导致遗漏，注射器这种最重要资源要是遗漏后续体验可以说是非常恶心。可以在进入地图有个查看当下地图资源，显示当下地图有哪些和有多少数量的资源。这说下地图指引问题；尤其是在有些在地图内可以选择被动技能下没有明显标识引导，从而错过该资源。 2.小地图内完完全全不显示在地图内的平台，导致寻找路程真是灾难性体验。有一次实验室找下一个房间的门我整整找5分钟。 3.小地图内不显示怪物，可以不显示普通怪但是一些精英怪得显示。 4.地图内存在着不必要的岔路和数量过少的传送门。在去下一个房间的门口附近没传送门，这还需要重新跑过去。在异变3可以算是完全不能接受的。 （2）.游戏设计问题 1.部分被动技能设计冗杂；下落攻击，滑铲攻击，油桶爆炸等一些触发困难也过于局限的被动技能下，我觉得可以直接转变成在专员的永久升级。而不是污染3选1的被动技能选择。 2.资源刷新有出现刷新不合理问题；什么叫做在地下室还给我刷新出普通品质武器，我回收都懒得回收。 3回收武器交互按键可以单独设计按键，每次长按好久然后一发现自己手里副武器掉落的整蛊感 （还未写完,继续玩继续寻找问题）

it is a good game, don't get me wrong but it feels like its trying to be dead cells a little too hard. neat premise and cool design, but the balance of skills are way off and some skills feel very... samey. you can reliably run the same loadout over and over if you don't add skills to the pool, and there's no incentive to go against that. a few skills aren't helpfully descriptive in terms of numbers. like... how many projectiles does this make? is the damage per projectile or total? how long do they last? why is the CD 0.0s when other passives dont list a CD? what's the ROF of the drone? why does damage amount matter when DPS is the more pressing issue? do the aether syringes affect the void sword, or just the katana syringes? what's my total +% numbers? do these things stack additively or multiplicatively? i just... can't get behind it. especially when pulse shield is basically necessary for some bosses lilifex >:(

Holy absolute peak gaming Batman. This is a fantastic cosmic horror themed roguelite about a ninja cyborg in space, what more is there to tell you? If you like Dead Cells and Hollow Knight you'll enjoy this, it's satisfying, gorgeous, and just all around a ton of fun. If I had to have some complaints, I would give two: the difficulty is questionable at times, my first time reaching the first boss I beat it first try, and that same run I managed to get the second boss down to under half health, so it's not super difficult. The other thing is that the meta progression, your out-of-run health, damage, stamina, etc. upgrades feels like it takes a long time to do, I didn't get my first health upgrade after five or so runs, which is something that should be upgradeable every two or three. Other than those? THis is peak fiction and a ton of fun to play, 9/10.

I don't think we've played the same game as all the reviewers. Maybe they are just too gentle considering the game's price or I don't know what is going on. If you enjoy no-brainer combat, sloppy level design and low-readable art; this is your game. - Combat mathematics are just badly designed. I don't even know how normal enemies attack, since they all just die in one slash or two. - Since Passive Skills also take up space in Skill slots, in the first 3-4 minutes of run, you are full of Skills and you just compare what to take and what to drop. - Item comparison UI is inefficient. It just shows whether the damage or that main stat of the new Item is more or not. It doesn't show the current Item's stat or what it currently does, so you can't be sure to replace it unless you take and redrop the item first. - Minimap is bad. It doesn't show dead ends, walls or obstacles. It just enlightens where you passed by, so you don't get much info by looking at it. - Enlarging the minimap is pointless. Enlarged minimap doesn't pan any way - it just gets bigger when you toggle it on, that's all. - It is hard to distinguish background from the foreground. Coloring, lights and shadows are not helpful. Especially in a level named "Gardens". Sometimes you don't even realize there is a wall or a platform until you bump or step on it by accident. I wasn't expecting much, considering the amount of reviews, but this was even below my expectations.

[h1] Hey, you. [/h1] Person scrubbing through for negative reviews because the positive ones make your eyes glaze over. I've got what you're looking for. The negative reviews you're most concerned about, the ones citing lack of depth or hooks, all have low playtime as a common factor, and this is the primary directing influence of those reviews. Not to say first impressions don't matter, those reviews are there for a reason, but they aren't missing these hooks because of a lack of them. They just didn't trust the process. All I can say is stick with it and you'll feel rewarded. If you're an old hand at roguelikes, you're gonna feel like there's a lot of technical detail in the combat that you're not having the opportunity to flex due to the enemies just dying immediately. Get the core loop down and secure that first win, after which the game opens up in earnest, and you'll have that chance. You'll get it. Additionally, if you're having trouble with the visual clarity, open up the accessibility settings and mess around with them. Those are there for your benefit, not for decoration.

This could have been a nice game in the veil of Dead Cells, unfortunately its poor design makes it impossible for me to recommend. The health system works well enough when facing common enemies, you have to be careful because any hit will take away your limited number of hit points. However, when facing bosses (who are bullet sponges) and there is a visual mess on screen (there is the huge boss itself, the multiple attacks he makes on screen and attacks that come off screen. Plus the change in lighting) that makes it hard to avoid damage and you die, even if you didn't take any damage the way to the boss. Because when you die you start at the base. So you have to go through WHOLE LEVELS before facing that boss again. When you die over and over this can get old really quickly. In Dark Souls this worked, because the boss fight wasn't that far away when you decided to retry it. In theory it gives you the option to pick up different skills and level up your stats a bit (both the temporary ones as well as the meta upgrades), but the more important upgrades (such as extra health syringes, etc.) require a special resource that apparently doesn't drop outside the boss fights. Meaning you are blocked from leveling at a certain point until you manage to clear the boss, whereas in Dark Souls you could always level up more to make up for the difference between you and the boss. Combine all of the above and this kind of loop becomes very unfun very fast.
It's a very shameless ripoff of dead-cells but less good.

Extremely annoying game. You tell us that you can parry attacks with an exclamation point, but when I try to do that on bosses, it doesn't even work, so you set me up for failure. This is trash design. At least change the exclamation point on the boss to red instead of the same as every other attack that you have conditioned me into parrying. It's really boring to only have 2 upgrade slots. Idk if you get more later but changing your abilities constantly just sucks, and a lot of the abilities, particularly the active ones, just f'ing suck compared to passive ones. I found the autoattacks in this game to be a bit unresponsive and sluggish. Some bosses have attacks you can't see coming and you have to die/lose HP to learn them which is unfair. This game doesn't have me convinced so I will refund.

Fantastic Aesthetic, Awesome space-horror setting, zero bugs, fast, responsive and enjoyable gameplay-loop AND the soundtrack slaps. I usually dont play many rogulikes, but this one makes me feel like I should. Only thing I would have liked to see more of were the story scenes, since the stuff thats there seems really interesting, tho wanting to play more of the game is hardly a negative. Katanaut is a fast-paced action roguelite that blends science-fiction horror, demanding combat, and rewarding progression into a compelling package. Developed by Voidmaw and published by Acclaim, Inc., the game places players aboard a massive space station that has fallen victim to a terrifying outbreak. What was once a thriving technological marvel has become a nightmare filled with mutated horrors, corrupted systems, and remnants of a civilization consumed by forces beyond its understanding. The game's premise immediately establishes a dark and mysterious atmosphere that serves as a strong foundation for the adventure that follows. At its core, Katanaut is driven by intense melee combat centered around precision, mobility, and quick decision-making. Armed primarily with a deadly katana, players must navigate dangerous environments while battling relentless enemies that punish careless mistakes. Combat encounters are designed to test reflexes and adaptability, requiring players to balance offense and defense while learning the attack patterns of increasingly dangerous foes. The responsiveness of the controls and the fluidity of movement create an engaging combat loop that remains satisfying throughout repeated runs. The roguelite structure plays a major role in maintaining long-term engagement. Every attempt through the station offers different challenges, enemy placements, and opportunities for growth. Death is not simply a setback but an essential part of progression. Through a narrative-driven resurrection system, players return stronger after each failure, gradually unlocking new abilities, talents, and upgrades. This approach creates a rewarding sense of advancement while preserving the tension that makes roguelites so addictive. Even unsuccessful runs contribute to future success, encouraging experimentation and persistence. Exploration is another highlight of the experience. The sprawling station is filled with interconnected zones that evolve in both visual design and threat level as players delve deeper into its depths. The environments effectively combine futuristic technology with grotesque cosmic horror influences, creating locations that feel both fascinating and unsettling. Hidden paths, valuable discoveries, and fragments of the station's history encourage players to thoroughly investigate their surroundings. This exploration element adds variety to the gameplay and helps the world feel more alive despite its catastrophic state. One of the game's most interesting features is the way it incorporates storytelling into progression. Scattered throughout the station are memory fragments left behind by former inhabitants. These fragments not only provide insight into the tragedy that unfolded but also contribute to character growth and gameplay development. Rather than relying heavily on lengthy exposition, Katanaut allows players to piece together its lore gradually, creating a sense of mystery that complements its horror themes. While the narrative is not the primary focus, it provides enough intrigue to keep players invested in uncovering the truth behind the station's downfall. Visually, Katanaut delivers an impressive presentation through detailed pixel art and strong environmental design. The contrast between sleek technological structures and horrific biological corruption creates a memorable aesthetic identity. Enemy designs are particularly effective, showcasing a variety of disturbing creatures that reinforce the game's cosmic horror influences. Combat effects are flashy without completely overwhelming the screen, and the animations contribute significantly to the feeling of speed and impact during battles. The audio design further strengthens the atmosphere. Ambient sounds create a constant sense of unease while exploring abandoned sections of the station, and the energetic soundtrack intensifies the action whenever combat erupts. Together, the visuals and audio create a cohesive experience that consistently reinforces the game's themes of survival, isolation, and discovery. The atmosphere remains one of Katanaut's strongest qualities, helping it stand out among many other roguelite releases. Despite its many strengths, Katanaut is not entirely without flaws. Some players may find the difficulty demanding, particularly during the early hours when available upgrades are limited. The story, while intriguing, occasionally takes a back seat to gameplay, leaving certain aspects of the world open to interpretation. However, these issues do little to diminish the overall quality of the experience, especially for players who prioritize challenging combat and replayability. Katanaut succeeds because it combines familiar genre elements into a polished and engaging adventure. Its blend of roguelite progression, challenging action combat, atmospheric exploration, and cosmic horror storytelling results in a game that feels both rewarding and memorable. Fans of difficult action games and replay-driven experiences will find plenty to appreciate, while the unique setting and strong presentation help distinguish it from many of its competitors. Rating: 8/10

[h1]Update after clearing final difficulty[/h1] That was quite the challenge and I think worth it overall once I found my ideal build. It does bring up that same issue I mentioned before were some abilities are seemingly straight butt no matter what you do. Single hit high cost abilities are very low worth. I ended up clearing with the plague ground or whatever that poisons in a giant AOE and you can stack it with the blade that lets you spam abilities, along with the shadow blade that rotates around you for low cost AOE clear. Supposedly there is a lifesteal ability that I never got around to unlocking but that would be nice. [h1] Original Review [/h1] A pretty decent roguelite all things considered. I see some reviews calling it a metroidvania but it is not a metroidvania in any way, I suppose because it's 2D and the maps you load into have some altering paths. It is not a metroidvania though, it is a roguelite through and through. Get your upgrades, get a lucky path that you can take in your build to start becoming ridiculously OP, and then push your luck for extreme upgrades to help you explode bosses. It's got a lot of the standard formula for roguelites. The big difference here is there is a lot of speed with your character and scaling feels pretty good if you get to invest heavily. My last run had a gun that normally deals 60-100 damage per shot dealing 900-1000 per shot and then critting for much more. It and some orbs I had were able to blow up bosses. The main story, or loosely what you could consider that, plays out over beating your runs across something like 4 increasing difficulties. Base, Warp 1, Warp 2, and Warp 3. In my time so far I've cleared Base and Warp 1, we'll see if I get around to Warp 2 and 3. The bosses get new abilities and levels get new modifers on higher difficulties along with you getting less access to healing. It's not substantially changing but it's doing some extra things the more you play which is good. It has a lot of pitfalls that your standard roguelites have as well where certain abilities seem pretty terrible, probably unless you get a very specific piece that can go crazy with it. The theme is great and it does a lot of heavy lifting.
